## Summary

Fixed the mass-assignment vulnerability in `app/Http/Controllers/PostController.ts`'s `update()` method: it previously called `Post.forceUpdate({ id: post.id }, await this.request.json())`, writing the *entire raw request body* straight to the database — bypassing both validation and the fillable allowlist, which is how a client could set `authorId` (or any other column like `createdAt`) directly.

The fix makes `update()` mirror `store()`'s pattern: `await this.validateBody(PostPayloadSchema)` (the same title/excerpt/body schema used for creation — required, with length limits, so empty titles are rejected with 422 again) followed by `Post.update({ id: post.id }, data)` — the allowlist-checked static, not `forceUpdate`, as defense-in-depth against `authorId` ever being written from request data. `Post.fillable` already excluded `authorId` (`app/Models/Post.ts`), so this closes the hole at both the validation layer (unknown keys silently dropped by Zod) and the model layer (unlisted keys would throw `MassAssignmentException`).

Added five tests to `tests/PostController.test.ts` covering: author cannot be changed via the request body, empty title is refused with 422 and leaves the post unchanged, out-of-schema fields (e.g. `createdAt`) aren't written, an ordinary author edit still works, and a non-author edit still gets 403. `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` both pass (7/7), and `bunx guren check` shows no new issues.
